title: IMF chief says AI risks may exceed opportunities without safeguards and ethical framework
source_used: Reuters, as relayed by The Financial Express, The News International and BigGo Finance (Reuters page itself returned HTTP 401)
key_facts: IMF Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva spoke on a panel at the IMF and World Bank annual meetings in Bangkok on Friday.
She said that without safeguards the risks of AI may exceed the opportunities, and that she is not sure society has an ethical foundation for it yet.
She backed a mix of industry self-regulation and government involvement, with the largest AI countries (the US, China, India) and supply-chain countries at the table.
She warned of negative shocks if AI's productivity gains do not arrive as fast as expected, and listed digital infrastructure, electricity and adequate regulation as preconditions for wide benefit.
Anthropic co-founder Jack Clark was on the same panel and said common-sense standards are needed.
US Treasury Undersecretary Erin Browne said at a separate news conference that the IMF is too focused on downside risks.
The Financial Express notes the IMF did not outline specific proposals and the discussion did not produce a detailed global rulebook.
quote_evidence: “If there are no safeguards, then the risks may exceed the opportunities. And above all, we do need an ethical foundation, and I’m not sure we are there as a society,” Georgieva said.
She backed a combination of industry self-regulation and government involvement, saying that policymakers may struggle to keep pace with rapid technological change.
Georgieva warned that AI could create economic risks if its promised productivity gains failed to materialise as quickly as businesses and investors expected.
why_it_matters_hint: The head of the IMF warns that AI-driven growth could turn into shocks without rules, while the US says the fund stresses the downside too much.
